headline: Apple leadership page updated as John Ternus becomes new CEO
summary: John Ternus has officially taken over as CEO of Apple, succeeding Tim Cook. The leadership page on Apple's website has been updated to reflect this change.
details: Apple has officially announced a significant leadership change, with John Ternus now listed as the company's Chief Executive Officer. This update comes as of September 1st.
Ternus succeeds Tim Cook, who has held the CEO position for many years. The change was reflected on Apple's official leadership page, indicating a formal transition.
While the article doesn't specify the reasons for the transition or Tim Cook's future role, the update signifies a new chapter for Apple's executive leadership.
John Ternus has been a key figure at Apple, previously leading the hardware engineering division. His promotion to CEO suggests a continued focus on product development and innovation.

headline_marked: [[CXMT begins risk production]] of HBM3E memory, aiming for mass production in 2027
headline: CXMT begins risk production of HBM3E memory, aiming for mass production in 2027
summary: China's DRAM champion ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has started risk production of HBM3E memory, a critical component for AI accelerators. This move could significantly reduce China's reliance on foreign memory manufacturers.
details: China's DRAM leader, CXMT, has reportedly begun risk production of HBM3E memory, marking a significant technological advancement. While still a generation behind the leading manufacturers producing HBM4, this milestone highlights CXMT's rapid progress in high-bandwidth memory technology.

Specifications for CXMT's HBM3E are not yet public, but JEDEC standards indicate potential data transfer rates up to 9.6 GT/s per pin and memory bandwidth reaching 1.228 TB/s. These stacks can offer capacities of 24GB or 36GB, depending on the number of DRAM dies used.

Several Chinese AI chip developers, including Alibaba Group's T-Head and Cambricon Technologies, are already evaluating CXMT's HBM3E. If testing is successful, these companies could integrate the memory into commercial products as early as next year.

The manufacturing of HBM is crucial for modern AI accelerators. CXMT's advancement in HBM3E production could lessen China's dependence on Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix for high-performance AI hardware, bolstering domestic capabilities.

Even though HBM3E is not the latest generation, it offers substantial bandwidth suitable for powerful AI accelerators, meeting the needs of many Chinese AI developers. This progress also signifies China's growing semiconductor ecosystem beyond commodity DRAM.

Geopolitically, this development is significant. With export restrictions limiting China's access to advanced AI processors and HBM, domestic production of accelerators and memory, combined with advanced packaging, moves China closer to semiconductor self-sufficiency.
